content.title: About
content.content: A low‑fat cereal or granola bar is a ready‑to‑eat snack made from whole grains, dried fruit, nuts and a small amount of sweetener. The product contains no added fat, making it suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first granola bar appeared in the United States in the 1970s as part of the health‑food movement.
Typical ingredients include oats, barley, rice flakes, honey, maple syrup and dried fruit.
Low‑fat versions often use puffed grains to keep volume without adding fat.
Bars are usually packaged in individual wrappers, convenient for on‑the‑go snacking.
In Russia these bars are popular among athletes and schoolchildren.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Whole grains and dried fruit provide fiber that supports normal digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes the product suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Oats and whole grains release glucose slowly, helping maintain steady energy levels.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Grain ingredients supply thiamine, niacin and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The bar can provide iron, magnesium and zinc, supporting blood health and immunity.

items.title: Allergy to nuts and dried fruit
items.content: The product may contain nuts, raisins, apricots or other common allergens.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Despite being fat‑free, many bars use honey or maple syrup, which raises the glycemic index.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: One bar can contain 150–250 kcal, so portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The bar is easy to carry in a bag, at work or at the gym. It can be eaten alone as a snack or chopped into yogurt, kefir or a smoothie to boost volume and nutrition.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in the original wrapper or an airtight container. For long‑term storage (over 6 months) keep refrigerated to prevent dried‑fruit spoilage.
